{{Short description|Italian mathematician (1498–1537)}}[[File:Galigai, Francesco – Pratica d'arithmetica, 1552 – BEIC IE7264584.jpg|thumb|''Pratica d'arithmetica'' (1552)]]

'''Francesco Galigai''', or '''Ghaligai''' ([[Florence]], 1498 – 1537), was an Italian [[mathematician]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://portal.dnb.de/opac.htm?method=simpleSearch&cqlMode=true&query=nid%3D1089408331|title=Galigai, Francesco|website=portal.dnb.de|publisher=[[German National Library]]|language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://data.cerl.org/thesaurus/cnp01235014|title=Galigai, Francesco|website=data.cerl.org|publisher=[[Consortium of European Research Libraries]]}}</ref>

In 1521, he published ''Summa de arithmetica'', a summary of contemporary knowledge on [[equation]]s of the first and second degree, including problems in [[indeterminate analysis]], along with notes on the history and development of mathematics in Italy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/francesco-galigai/|title=Galigài, Francesco|website=treccani.it|publisher=[[Treccani]]|language=it}}</ref>
